column16: Name: g and s written plain (no Windows-1252 form of ğ ş). Club renamed Hacettepe SK on 18 July 2008. Stadium: Transfermarkt match sheets show home league games at Cebeci Inönü Stadium (I with dot written plain), capacity 15000 from en.wikipedia Cebeci Inönü Stadium page only, no second source. Colours red and black from en and tr Wikipedia (Gençlerbirligi colours 2003 to 2008), no second source. Founded: en.wikipedia gives 1949, tr.wikipedia gives 1947 (as Sanayi Barbarosspor), refounded 2001 as Asasspor, unresolved. Row is right: RSSSF tur07 lists Gençlerbirligi Oftas Ankara 1st in 2. Lig A, promoted.

Named Sibir from 2006 (Chkalovets-1936 up to 2005). Finished 3rd. Stadium from Transfermarkt 2007 match sheets (Spartak). Capacity 12500 from Wikipedia infobox and Transfermarkt club page (current figure, not the 2007 figure). Colours from the current Wikipedia kit, 2007 kit not confirmed (inference).

Club withdrew on 23 July 2007 for lack of money and was dissolved (RSSSF), row is right but the club did not finish the season. Stadium: CSK Stadium per en and ru Wikipedia, Transfermarkt match sheets show CSK for most home games and Agrokomplekt for the first two. Capacity: 25000 is the figure after the 2008 refurbishment, 2007 figure unknown. Colours from Wikipedia kit only, no second source. Transfermarkt spells the name Spartak-MZK Ryazan.

Club moved from Chelyabinsk (Spartak Chelyabinsk, founded 2000 as Lukoil Chelyabinsk) to Nizhny Novgorod for 2006 (RSSSF agrees). Finished 18th and was relegated, dissolved 2007. Stadium from Transfermarkt 2006 match sheets (Zentralstadion Lokomotiv). Capacity 17856 from Wikipedia stadium page only (renovated 1997), no second source. Colours from Wikipedia kit only. RSSSF and Transfermarkt spell Nizhniy.

Entered the First Division in 2009 from 3rd place in Second Division zone South after other clubs refused promotion (RSSSF and Wikipedia agree). Finished 10th. Stadium: Kuban per the 2009 season page, Transfermarkt match sheets show most home games at Kuban, some at Trud Stadium (3000), and three marked OZON Arena, which did not exist in 2009 (a Transfermarkt error, inference). Capacity 35200 from the 2009 season page only, the Kuban page gives 31654 after later renovation. Colours black and green from the club nickname (The Black-Greens), 2009 kit not confirmed (inference). Founded 22 February 2008.

This is FC Nizhny Novgorod founded 2007 (merged into Volga in 2012), not Volga Nizhny Novgorod. Entered 2009 from 3rd place in Second Division zone Ural-Povolzhye after other clubs refused (RSSSF agrees). Finished 13th. Stadium from Transfermarkt 2009 match sheets (Severny). Capacity: Wikipedia 3180, Transfermarkt 4500 (current figure), kept 3180. Colours from Wikipedia kit only (black shirts, sky blue). RSSSF and Transfermarkt spell Nizhniy.
